messages.subject: way way behind
parts:
I'm so far behind on the dev list that I don't know
whether I'm coming or going.

If anyone specifically needs my help on something other than
sorting out our long-term process, which is my only priority
right now, could you send me e-mail rather than pushing it
through GitHub?

I'd personally rather not have to think about code until
we have a process for managing it down.

Until then, sorry to slow development down.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: way way behind
parts:
On Wednesday, May 15, 2013 3:47:32 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I'm so far behind on the dev list that I don't know
whether I'm coming or going.

To summarize a bit:

-- I think several people like gitflow and no one seems to be opposed. To transition to gitflow, we need to get master stable enough to release a new Stan and then immediately branch the development branch off of master. An issue is that we currently have a few public feature-ish branches and who knows how many local branches that have already branched from master. These will become inconsistent with gitflow where nothing branches off of master with the one-time exception of the development branch. So, those orphaned branches will have to be dealt with in one of several ways. But I think no one should start any nontrivial new branches right now.

-- Restricting permission to merge into master or development is workable. In the worst case, we could make a separate repo on GitHub for those two branches, but I think having a pre-push hook locally will work too.

-- On the remote testing front, I got a mostly favorable email about doing this on Hotfoot. But I think that is only going to be possible for Columbia affiliates and is only one toolchain. So, we might need to look into Amazon EC2 in addition.

The good news is that master is in pretty good shape at the moment.

Ben
